verses.text: The vision of Isai'ah the son of A'moz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzzi'ah, Jo'tham, A'haz, and Hezeki'ah, kings of Judah.
Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth;
The ox knows its owner,
Ah, sinful nation,
Why will you still be struck down,
From the sole of the foot even to the head,
Your country lies desolate,
And the daughter of Zion is left
If the LORD of hosts
Hear the word of the LORD,
“What to me is the multitude of your sacrifices?
“When you come to appear before me,
Bring no more vain offerings;
Your new moons and your appointed feasts
When you spread forth your hands,
Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean;
learn to do good;
“Come now, let us reason together,
If you are willing and obedient,
but if you refuse and rebel,
How the faithful city
Your silver has become dross,
Your princes are rebels
Therefore the Lord says,
I will turn my hand against you
And I will restore your judges as at the first,
Zion shall be redeemed by justice,
But rebels and sinners shall be destroyed together,
For you shall be ashamed of the oaks
For you shall be like an oak
And the strong shall become tow,
The word which Isai'ah the son of A'moz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
It shall come to pass in the latter days
and many peoples shall come, and say:
He shall judge between the nations,
O house of Jacob,
For you have rejected your people,
Their land is filled with silver and gold,
Their land is filled with idols;
So man is humbled,
Enter into the rock,
The haughty looks of man shall be brought low,
For the LORD of hosts has a day
against all the cedars of Lebanon,
against all the high mountains,
against every high tower,
against all the ships of Tar'shish,
And the haughtiness of man shall be humbled,
And the idols shall utterly pass away.
And men shall enter the caves of the rocks
In that day men will cast forth
to enter the caverns of the rocks and the clefts of the cliffs,
Turn away from man
For behold, the Lord, the LORD of hosts,
the mighty man and the soldier,
the captain of fifty
And I will make boys their princes,
And the people will oppress one another,
When a man takes hold of his brother
in that day he will speak out, saying:
For Jerusalem has stumbled,
Their partiality witnesses against them;
Tell the righteous that it shall be well with them,
Woe to the wicked! It shall be ill with him,
My people—children are their oppressors,
The LORD has taken his place to contend,
The LORD enters into judgment
What do you mean by crushing my people,
The LORD said:
the Lord will strike with a scab
the pendants, the bracelets, and the scarfs;
the headdresses, the armlets, the sashes, the perfume boxes, and the amulets;
the signet rings and nose rings;
the festal robes, the mantles, the cloaks, and the handbags;
the garments of gauze, the linen garments, the turbans, and the veils.
Instead of perfume there will be rottenness;
Your men shall fall by the sword
And her gates shall lament and mourn;
And seven women shall take hold of one man in that day, saying, “We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes, only let us be called by your name; take away our reproach.”
In that day the branch of the LORD shall be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land shall be the pride and glory of the survivors of Israel.
And he who is left in Zion and remains in Jerusalem will be called holy, every one who has been recorded for life in Jerusalem,
when the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and cleansed the bloodstains of Jerusalem from its midst by a spirit of judgment and by a spirit of burning.

Then the LORD will create over the whole site of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day, and smoke and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory there will be a canopy and a pavilion.
It will be for a shade by day from the heat, and for a refuge and a shelter from the storm and rain.
Let me sing for my beloved
He dug it and cleared it of stones,
And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem
What more was there to do for my vineyard,
And now I will tell you
I will make it a waste;
For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts
Woe to those who join house to house,
The LORD of hosts has sworn in my hearing:
For ten acres of vineyard shall yield but one bath,
Woe to those who rise early in the morning,
They have lyre and harp,
Therefore my people go into exile for want of knowledge;
Therefore Sheol has enlarged its appetite
Man is bowed down, and men are brought low,
But the LORD of hosts is exalted in justice,
Then shall the lambs graze as in their pasture,
Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood,
who say: “Let him make haste,
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil,
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes,
Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine,
who acquit the guilty for a bribe,
Therefore, as the tongue of fire devours the stubble,
Therefore the anger of the LORD was kindled against his people,
He will raise a signal for a nation afar off,
None is weary, none stumbles,
their arrows are sharp,
Their roaring is like a lion,
They will growl over it on that day,
In the year that King Uzzi'ah died I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.
Above him stood the seraphim; each had six wings: with two he covered his face, and with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.
And one called to another and said:
And the foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him who called, and the house was filled with smoke.
And I said: “Woe is me! For I am lost; for I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts!”
And he touched my mouth, and said: “Behold, this has touched your lips; your guilt is taken away, and your sin forgiven.”
And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here am I! Send me.”
And he said, “Go, and say to this people:
Make the heart of this people fat,
Then I said, “How long, O Lord?”
and the LORD removes men far away,
And though a tenth remain in it,

In the days of A'haz the son of Jo'tham, son of Uzzi'ah, king of Judah, Re'zin the king of Syria and Pe'kah the son of Remali'ah the king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to wage war against it, but they could not conquer it.
When the house of David was told, “Syria is in league with E'phraim,” his heart and the heart of his people shook as the trees of the forest shake before the wind.

and say to him, ‘Take heed, be quiet, do not fear, and do not let your heart be faint because of these two smoldering stumps of firebrands, at the fierce anger of Re'zin and Syria and the son of Remali'ah.
Because Syria, with E'phraim and the son of Remali'ah, has devised evil against you, saying,
“Let us go up against Judah and terrify it, and let us conquer it for ourselves, and set up the son of Ta'be-el as king in the midst of it,”
thus says the Lord GOD:
For the head of Syria is Damascus,
And the head of E'phraim is Samar'ia,
Then the LORD said to me, “Take a large tablet and write upon it in common characters, ‘Belonging to Ma'her-shal'al-hash''-baz.’ ”
And I got reliable witnesses, Uri'ah the priest and Zechari'ah the son of Jeberechi'ah, to attest for me.
And I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. Then the LORD said to me, “Call his name Ma'her-shal'al-hash''-baz;
for before the child knows how to cry ‘My father’ or ‘My mother,’ the wealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samar'ia will be carried away before the king of Assyria.”
“Because this people have refused the waters of Shilo'ah that flow gently, and melt in fear before Re'zin and the son of Remali'ah;

therefore, behold, the Lord is bringing up against them the waters of the River, mighty and many, the king of Assyria and all his glory; and it will rise over all its channels and go over all its banks;
and it will sweep on into Judah, it will overflow and pass on, reaching even to the neck; and its outspread wings will fill the breadth of your land, O Imman'u-el.”
Be broken, you peoples, and be dismayed;
Take counsel together, but it will come to nought;
“Do not call conspiracy all that this people call conspiracy, and do not fear what they fear, nor be in dread.
But the LORD of hosts, him you shall regard as holy; let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.
And he will become a sanctuary, and a stone of offense, and a rock of stumbling to both houses of Israel, a trap and a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And many shall stumble thereon; they shall fall and be broken; they shall be snared and taken.”

But there will be no gloom for her that was in anguish. In the former time he brought into contempt the land of Zeb'ulun and the land of Naph'tali, but in the latter time he will make glorious the way of the sea, the land beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
The people who walked in darkness
You have multiplied the nation,
For the yoke of his burden,
For every boot of the tramping warrior in battle tumult
For to us a child is born,
Of the increase of his government and of peace
The Lord has sent a word against Jacob,
and all the people will know,
“The bricks have fallen,
So the LORD raises adversaries against them,
The Syrians on the east and the Philis'tines on the west
The people did not turn to him who struck them,
So the LORD cut off from Israel head and tail,
the elder and honored man is the head,
for those who lead this people lead them astray,
Therefore the Lord does not rejoice over their young men,
For wickedness burns like a fire,
Through the wrath of the LORD of hosts
They snatch on the right, but are still hungry,
Manas'seh E'phraim, and Ephraim Manasseh,
Again the LORD spoke to A'haz,
“Ask a sign of the LORD your God; let it be deep as Sheol or high as heaven.”
But A'haz said, “I will not ask, and I will not put the LORD to the test.”
And he said, “Hear then, O house of David! Is it too little for you to weary men, that you weary my God also?
Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Imman'u-el.
He shall eat curds and honey when he knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good.
For before the child knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land before whose two kings you are in dread will be deserted.
The LORD will bring upon you and upon your people and upon your father’s house such days as have not come since the day that E'phraim departed from Judah—the king of Assyria.”
And they will all come and settle in the steep ravines, and in the clefts of the rocks, and on all the thornbushes, and on all the pastures.
and because of the abundance of milk which they give, he will eat curds; for every one that is left in the land will eat curds and honey.
With bow and arrows men will come there, for all the land will be briers and thorns;
and as for all the hills which used to be hoed with a hoe, you will not come there for fear of briers and thorns; but they will become a place where cattle are let loose and where sheep tread.
There shall come forth a shoot from the stump of Jesse,
And the Spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him,
And his delight shall be in the fear of the LORD.
but with righteousness he shall judge the poor,
Righteousness shall be the belt of his waist,
The wolf shall dwell with the lamb,
The cow and the bear shall feed;
The sucking child shall play over the hole of the asp,
They shall not hurt or destroy
In that day the root of Jesse shall stand as an ensign to the peoples; him shall the nations seek, and his dwellings shall be glorious.
He will raise an ensign for the nations,
The jealousy of E'phraim shall depart,
But they shall swoop down upon the shoulder of the Philis'tines in the west,
And the LORD will utterly destroy
And there will be a highway from Assyria
You will say in that day:
“Behold, God is my salvation;
And you will say in that day:
“Sing praises to the LORD, for he has done gloriously;
Shout, and sing for joy, O inhabitant of Zion,
The oracle concerning Babylon which Isai'ah the son of A'moz saw.
On a bare hill raise a signal,
I myself have commanded my consecrated ones,
Listen, a tumult on the mountains
They come from a distant land,
Wail, for the day of the LORD is near;
Therefore all hands will be feeble,
and they will be dismayed.
Behold, the day of the LORD comes,
For the stars of the heavens and their constellations
I will punish the world for its evil,
I will make men more rare than fine gold,
Therefore I will make the heavens tremble,
And like a hunted gazelle,
Whoever is found will be thrust through,
Their infants will be dashed in pieces
Behold, I am stirring up the Medes against them,
Their bows will slaughter the young men;
And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms,
It will never be inhabited
But wild beasts will lie down there,
Hyenas will cry in its towers,
The LORD will have compassion on Jacob and will again choose Israel, and will set them in their own land, and strangers will join them and will cling to the house of Jacob.

And the peoples will take them and bring them to their place, and the house of Israel will possess them in the LORD’s land as male and female slaves; they will take captive those who were their captors, and rule over those who oppressed them.
you will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon:
The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked,
that struck the peoples in wrath
The whole earth is at rest and quiet;
The cypresses rejoice at you,
Sheol beneath is stirred up
All of them will speak
Your pomp is brought down to Sheol,
“How you are fallen from heaven,
You said in your heart,
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds,
But you are brought down to Sheol,
Those who see you will stare at you,
who made the world like a desert
All the kings of the nations lie in glory,
but you are cast out, away from your sepulchre,
You will not be joined with them in burial,
Prepare slaughter for his sons
And I will make it a possession of the hedgehog, and pools of water, and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction, says the LORD of hosts.”
The LORD of hosts has sworn:
that I will break the Assyrian in my land,
This is the purpose that is purposed
For the LORD of hosts has purposed,
In the year that King A'haz died came this oracle:
“Rejoice not, O Philis'tia, all of you,
And the first-born of the poor will feed,
Wail, O gate; cry, O city;
What will one answer the messengers of the nation?
An oracle concerning Moab.
The daughter of Di'bon has gone up
in the streets they put on sackcloth;
Heshbon and E''lea'leh cry out,
My heart cries out for Moab;
the waters of Nimrim
Therefore the abundance they have gained
For a cry has gone
For the waters of Di'bon are full of blood;
And joy and gladness are taken away
Therefore my soul moans like a lyre for Moab,

But now the LORD says, “In three years, like the years of a hireling, the glory of Moab will be brought into contempt, in spite of all his great multitude, and those who survive will be very few and feeble.”
Bind up the testimony, seal the teaching among my disciples.
I will wait for the LORD, who is hiding his face from the house of Jacob, and I will hope in him.
Behold, I and the children whom the LORD has given me are signs and portents in Israel from the LORD of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
And when they say to you, “Consult the mediums and the wizards who chirp and mutter,” should not a people consult their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?
To the teaching and to the testimony! Surely for this word which they speak there is no dawn.
They will pass through the land, greatly distressed and hungry; and when they are hungry, they will be enraged and will curse their king and their God, and turn their faces upward;
and they will look to the earth, but behold, distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish; and they will be thrust into thick darkness.
An oracle concerning Damascus.
Her cities will be deserted for ever;
The fortress will disappear from E'phraim,
And in that day
And it shall be as when the reaper gathers standing grain
Gleanings will be left in it,
they will not have regard for the altars, the work of their hands, and they will not look to what their own fingers have made, either the Ashe'rim or the altars of incense.
For you have forgotten the God of your salvation,
though you make them grow on the day that you plant them,
Ah, the thunder of many peoples,
The nations roar like the roaring of many waters,
At evening time, behold, terror!
Ah, land of whirring wings
which sends ambassadors by the Nile,
All you inhabitants of the world,
For thus the LORD said to me:
For before the harvest, when the blossom is over,
They shall all of them be left
An oracle concerning Egypt.
And I will stir up Egyptians against Egyptians,
and the spirit of the Egyptians within them will be emptied out,
and I will give over the Egyptians
And the waters of the Nile will be dried up,
and its canals will become foul,
There will be bare places by the Nile,
The fishermen will mourn and lament,
The workers in combed flax will be in despair,
Those who are the pillars of the land will be crushed,
The princes of Zoan are utterly foolish;
Where then are your wise men?
The princes of Zoan have become fools,
The LORD has mingled within her a spirit of confusion;
And there will be nothing for Egypt
And the land of Judah will become a terror to the Egyptians; every one to whom it is mentioned will fear because of the purpose which the LORD of hosts has purposed against them.
It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt; when they cry to the LORD because of oppressors he will send them a savior, and will defend and deliver them.

And the LORD will make himself known to the Egyptians; and the Egyptians will know the LORD in that day and worship with sacrifice and burnt offering, and they will make vows to the LORD and perform them.
And the LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing, and they will return to the LORD, and he will heed their supplications and heal them.
whom the LORD of hosts has blessed, saying, “Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my heritage.”
In that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no more lean upon him that struck them, but will lean upon the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God.
For though your people Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them will return. Destruction is decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
For the Lord, the LORD of hosts, will make a full end, as decreed, in the midst of all the earth.
For in a very little while my indignation will come to an end, and my anger will be directed to their destruction.
And the LORD of hosts will wield against them a scourge, as when he struck Mid'ian at the rock of Or'eb; and his rod will be over the sea, and he will lift it as he did in Egypt.
And in that day his burden will depart from your shoulder, and his yoke will be destroyed from your neck.”
he has come to Ai'ath;
they have crossed over the pass,
Cry aloud, O daughter of Gallim!
Madme'nah is in flight,
This very day he will halt at Nob,
Behold, the Lord, the LORD of hosts
He will cut down the thickets of the forest with an axe,
The oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea.
A stern vision is told to me;
Therefore my loins are filled with anguish;
My mind reels, horror has appalled me;
They prepare the table,
For thus the Lord said to me:
When he sees riders, horsemen in pairs,
Then he who saw cried:
And, behold, here come riders,
O my threshed and winnowed one,
The oracle concerning Du'mah.
The watchman says:
The oracle concerning Arabia.
To the thirsty bring water,
For they have fled from the swords,
and the remainder of the archers of the mighty men of the sons of Ke'dar will be few; for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.”
The oracle concerning the valley of vision.
you who are full of shoutings,
All your rulers have fled together,
Therefore I said:
For the Lord GOD of hosts has a day
And E'lam bore the quiver
Your choicest valleys were full of chariots,
He has taken away the covering of Judah.
and you saw that the breaches of the city of David were many, and you collected the waters of the lower pool,
and you counted the houses of Jerusalem, and you broke down the houses to fortify the wall.
You made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you did not look to him who did it, or have regard for him who planned it long ago.
In that day the Lord GOD of hosts
and behold, joy and gladness,
The LORD of hosts has revealed himself in my ears:
What have you to do here and whom have you here, that you have hewn here a tomb for yourself, you who hew a tomb on the height, and carve a habitation for yourself in the rock?
Behold, the LORD will hurl you away violently, O you strong man. He will seize firm hold on you,
and whirl you round and round, and throw you like a ball into a wide land; there you shall die, and there shall be your splendid chariots, you shame of your master’s house.
I will thrust you from your office, and you will be cast down from your station.
In that day I will call my servant Eli'akim the son of Hilki'ah,
and I will clothe him with your robe, and will bind your belt on him, and will commit your authority to his hand; and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
And I will place on his shoulder the key of the house of David; he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.
And I will fasten him like a peg in a sure place, and he will become a throne of honor to his father’s house.
And they will hang on him the whole weight of his father’s house, the offspring and issue, every small vessel, from the cups to all the flagons.

In that day, says the LORD of hosts, the peg that was fastened in a sure place will give way; and it will be cut down and fall, and the burden that was upon it will be cut off, for the LORD has spoken.”
The oracle concerning Tyre.
Be still, O inhabitants of the coast,
and were on many waters;
Be ashamed, O Si'don, for the sea has spoken,
When the report comes to Egypt,
Pass over to Tar'shish,
Is this your exultant city
Who has purposed this
The LORD of hosts has purposed it,
Overflow your land like the Nile,
He has stretched out his hand over the sea,
And he said:
Wail, O ships of Tar'shish,
In that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the harlot:
“Take a harp,
At the end of seventy years, the LORD will visit Tyre, and she will return to her hire, and will play the harlot with all the kingdoms of the world upon the face of the earth.
Her merchandise and her hire will be dedicated to the LORD; it will not be stored or hoarded, but her merchandise will supply abundant food and fine clothing for those who dwell before the LORD.
Behold, the LORD will lay waste the earth and make it desolate,
And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest;
The earth shall be utterly laid waste and utterly despoiled;
The earth mourns and withers,
The earth lies polluted
Therefore a curse devours the earth,
The wine mourns,
The mirth of the timbrels is stilled,
No more do they drink wine with singing;
The city of chaos is broken down,
There is an outcry in the streets for lack of wine;
Desolation is left in the city,
For thus it shall be in the midst of the earth
They lift up their voices, they sing for joy;
Therefore in the east give glory to the LORD;
From the ends of the earth we hear songs of praise,
Terror, and the pit, and the snare are upon you, O inhabitant of the earth!
He who flees at the sound of the terror
The earth is utterly broken,
The earth staggers like a drunken man,
On that day the LORD will punish
They will be gathered together
Then the moon will be confounded,
O LORD, you are my God;
For you have made the city a heap,
Therefore strong peoples will glorify you;
For you have been a stronghold to the poor,
like heat in a dry place.
And he will destroy on this mountain the covering that is cast over all peoples, the veil that is spread over all nations.
He will swallow up death for ever, and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from all faces, and the reproach of his people he will take away from all the earth, for the LORD has spoken.
For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain, and Moab shall be trodden down in his place, as straw is trodden down in a dung-pit.
And he will spread out his hands in the midst of it as a swimmer spreads his hands out to swim; but the LORD will lay low his pride together with the skill of his hands.
And the high fortifications of his walls he will bring down, lay low, and cast to the ground, even to the dust.
In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah:
Open the gates,
You keep him in perfect peace,
Trust in the LORD for ever,
For he has brought low
The foot tramples it,
The way of the righteous is level;
In the path of your judgments,
My soul yearns for you in the night,
If favor is shown to the wicked,
O LORD, your hand is lifted up,
O LORD, you will ordain peace for us,
O LORD our God,
They are dead, they will not live;
But you have increased the nation, O LORD,
O LORD, in distress they sought you,
Like a woman with child,
we were with child, we writhed,
Your dead shall live, their bodies shall rise.
Come, my people, enter your chambers,
For behold, the LORD is coming forth out of his place
In that day the LORD with his hard and great and strong sword will punish Levi'athan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the twisting serpent, and he will slay the dragon that is in the sea.
In that day:
I, the LORD, am its keeper;
I have no wrath.
Or let them lay hold of my protection,
In days to come Jacob shall take root,
Has he struck them down as he struck those who struck them?
Measure by measure, by exile you contended with them;
Therefore by this the guilt of Jacob will be expiated,
For the fortified city is solitary,
When its boughs are dry, they are broken;
In that day from the river Euphra'tes to the Brook of Egypt the LORD will thresh out the grain, and you will be gathered one by one, O people of Israel.

And in that day a great trumpet will be blown, and those who were lost in the land of Assyria and those who were driven out to the land of Egypt will come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain at Jerusalem.
Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of E'phraim,
Behold, the Lord has one who is mighty and strong;
The proud crown of the drunkards of E'phraim
and the fading flower of its glorious beauty,
In that day the LORD of hosts will be a crown of glory,
and a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment,
These also reel with wine
For all tables are full of vomit,
“Whom will he teach knowledge,
For it is precept upon precept, precept upon precept,
No, but by men of strange lips
to whom he has said,
Therefore the word of the LORD will be to them
Therefore hear the word of the LORD, you scoffers,
Because you have said, “We have made a covenant with death,
therefore thus says the Lord GOD,
And I will make justice the line,
Then your covenant with death will be annulled,
As often as it passes through it will take you;
For the bed is too short to stretch oneself on it,
For the LORD will rise up as on Mount Pera'zim,
Now therefore do not scoff,
Give ear, and hear my voice;
Does he who plows for sowing plow continually?
When he has leveled its surface,
For he is instructed rightly;
Dill is not threshed with a threshing sledge,
Does one crush bread grain?
This also comes from the LORD of hosts;
Ho Ar'iel, Ariel,
Yet I will distress Ar'iel,
And I will encamp against you round about,
Then deep from the earth you shall speak,
But the multitude of your foes shall be like small dust,
you will be visited by the LORD of hosts
And the multitude of all the nations that fight against Ar'iel,
As when a hungry man dreams he is eating
Stupefy yourselves and be in a stupor,
For the LORD has poured out upon you
And when they give the book to one who cannot read, saying, “Read this,” he says, “I cannot read.”
And the Lord said:
therefore, behold, I will again
Woe to those who hide deep from the LORD their counsel,
You turn things upside down!
Is it not yet a very little while
In that day the deaf shall hear the words of a book,
The meek shall obtain fresh joy in the LORD,
For the ruthless shall come to nothing and the scoffer cease,
who by a word make a man out to be an offender,
For when he sees his children,
And those who err in spirit will come to understanding,
“Woe to the rebellious children,” says the LORD,
who set out to go down to Egypt,
Therefore the protection of Pharaoh shall turn to your shame,
For though his officials are at Zoan
every one comes to shame
An oracle on the beasts of the Neg'eb.
For Egypt’s help is worthless and empty,
And now, go, write it before them on a tablet,
For they are a rebellious people,
who say to the seers, “See not”;
leave the way, turn aside from the path,
Therefore thus says the Holy One of Israel,
therefore this iniquity shall be to you
and its breaking is like that of a potter’s vessel
For thus said the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel,
but you said,
A thousand shall flee at the threat of one,
Therefore the LORD waits to be gracious to you;
And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your Teacher will not hide himself any more, but your eyes shall see your Teacher.
And your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying, “This is the way, walk in it,” when you turn to the right or when you turn to the left.
Then you will defile your silver-covered graven images and your gold-plated molten images. You will scatter them as unclean things; you will say to them, “Begone!”
and the oxen and the donkeys that till the ground will eat salted food, which has been winnowed with shovel and fork.
And upon every lofty mountain and every high hill there will be brooks running with water, in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

Moreover the light of the moon will be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day when the LORD binds up the hurt of his people, and heals the wounds inflicted by his blow.
Behold, the name of the LORD comes from far,
his breath is like an overflowing stream
And the LORD will cause his majestic voice to be heard and the descending blow of his arm to be seen, in furious anger and a flame of devouring fire, with a cloudburst and tempest and hailstones.
The Assyrians will be terror-stricken at the voice of the LORD, when he strikes with his rod.
And every stroke of the staff of punishment which the LORD lays upon them will be to the sound of timbrels and lyres; battling with brandished arm he will fight with them.

For a burning place has long been prepared; yes, for the king it is made ready, its pyre made deep and wide, with fire and wood in abundance; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, kindles it.
Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help
And yet he is wise and brings disaster,
The Egyptians are men, and not God;
For thus the LORD said to me,
Like birds hovering, so the LORD of hosts
For in that day every one shall cast away his idols of silver and his idols of gold, which your hands have sinfully made for you.
“And the Assyrian shall fall by a sword, not of man;
His rock shall pass away in terror,
Behold, a king will reign in righteousness,
Each will be like a hiding place from the wind,
Then the eyes of those who see will not be closed,
The mind of the rash will have good judgment,
The fool will no more be called noble,
For the fool speaks folly,
The knaveries of the knave are evil;
But he who is noble devises noble things,
Rise up, you women who are at ease, hear my voice;
In little more than a year
Tremble, you women who are at ease,
Beat upon your breasts for the pleasant fields,
for the soil of my people
For the palace will be forsaken,
until the Spirit is poured upon us from on high,
Then justice will dwell in the wilderness,
And the effect of righteousness will be peace,
My people will abide in a peaceful habitation,
And the forest will utterly go down,
Happy are you who sow beside all waters,
Woe to you, destroyer,
O LORD, be gracious to us; we wait for you.
At the thunderous noise peoples flee,
and spoil is gathered as the caterpillar gathers;
The LORD is exalted, for he dwells on high;
and he will be the stability of your times,
Behold, the valiant ones cry without;
The highways lie waste,
The land mourns and languishes;
“Now I will arise,” says the LORD,
You conceive chaff, you bring forth stubble;
And the peoples will be as if burned to lime,
Hear, you who are far off, what I have done;
The sinners in Zion are afraid;
He who walks righteously and speaks uprightly,
he will dwell on the heights;
Your eyes will see the king in his beauty;
Your mind will muse on the terror:
You will see no more the insolent people,
Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts!
But there the LORD in majesty will be for us
For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our ruler,
Your tackle hangs loose;
And no inhabitant will say, “I am sick”;
Draw near, O nations, to hear,
For the LORD is enraged against all the nations,
Their slain shall be cast out,
All the host of heaven shall rot away,
For my sword has drunk its fill in the heavens;
The LORD has a sword; it is sated with blood,
Wild oxen shall fall with them,
For the LORD has a day of vengeance,
And the streams of E'dom shall be turned into pitch,
Night and day it shall not be quenched;
But the hawk and the porcupine shall possess it,
They shall name it No Kingdom There,
Thorns shall grow over its strongholds,
And wild beasts shall meet with hyenas,
There shall the owl nest and lay
Seek and read from the book of the LORD:
He has cast the lot for them,
The wilderness and the dry land shall be glad,
it shall blossom abundantly,
Strengthen the weak hands,
Say to those who are of a fearful heart,
Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened,
then shall the lame man leap like a deer,
the burning sand shall become a pool,
And a highway shall be there,
No lion shall be there,
And the ransomed of the LORD shall return,
In the fourteenth year of King Hezeki'ah, Sennach'erib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and took them.
And the king of Assyria sent the Rab'shakeh from La'chish to King Hezeki'ah at Jerusalem, with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool on the highway to the Fuller’s Field.
And there came out to him Eli'akim the son of Hilki'ah, who was over the household, and Shebna the secretary, and Jo'ah the son of A'saph, the recorder.
Do you think that mere words are strategy and power for war? On whom do you now rely, that you have rebelled against me?
Behold, you are relying on Egypt, that broken reed of a staff, which will pierce the hand of any man who leans on it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who rely on him.
But if you say to me, “We rely on the LORD our God,” is it not he whose high places and altars Hezeki'ah has removed, saying to Judah and to Jerusalem, “You shall worship before this altar”?
Come now, make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to set riders upon them.
How then can you repulse a single captain among the least of my master’s servants, when you rely on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
Moreover, is it without the LORD that I have come up against this land to destroy it? The LORD said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.’ ”

But the Rab'shakeh said, “Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are doomed with you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?”
Thus says the king: ‘Do not let Hezeki'ah deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you.
Do not let Hezeki'ah make you rely on the LORD by saying, “The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.”

Do not listen to Hezeki'ah; for thus says the king of Assyria: Make your peace with me and come out to me; then every one of you will eat of his own vine, and every one of his own fig tree, and every one of you will drink the water of his own cistern;
until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
Beware lest Hezeki'ah mislead you by saying, “The LORD will deliver us.” Has any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Ha'math and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharva'im? Have they delivered Samar'ia out of my hand?
Who among all the gods of these countries have delivered their countries out of my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?’ ”

Then Eli'akim the son of Hilki'ah, who was over the household, and Sheb'na the secretary, and Jo'ah the son of A'saph, the recorder, came to Hezeki'ah with their clothes torn, and told him the words of the Rab'shakeh.
When King Hezeki'ah heard it, he tore his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
And he sent Eli'akim, who was over the household, and Shebna the secretary, and the senior priests, clothed with sackcloth, to the prophet Isai'ah the son of A'moz.
They said to him, “Thus says Hezeki'ah, ‘This day is a day of distress, of rebuke, and of disgrace; children have come to the birth, and there is no strength to bring them forth.

It may be that the LORD your God heard the words of the Rab'shakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to mock the living God, and will rebuke the words which the LORD your God has heard; therefore lift up your prayer for the remnant that is left.’ ”
Isai'ah said to them, “Say to your master, ‘Thus says the LORD: Do not be afraid because of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have reviled me.
Behold, I will put a spirit in him, so that he shall hear a rumor, and return to his own land; and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.’ ”
Now the king heard concerning Tirha'kah king of Ethiopia, “He has set out to fight against you.” And when he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezeki'ah, saying,
“Thus shall you speak to Hezeki'ah king of Judah: ‘Do not let your God on whom you rely deceive you by promising that Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.
Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, destroying them utterly. And shall you be delivered?
Have the gods of the nations delivered them, the nations which my fathers destroyed, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telas'sar?
Where is the king of Ha'math, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharva'im, the king of He'na, or the king of Ivvah?’ ”
And Hezeki'ah prayed to the LORD:
“O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, who are enthroned above the cherubim, you are the God, you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made heaven and earth.
Incline your ear, O LORD, and hear; open your eyes, O LORD, and see; and hear all the words of Sennach'erib, which he has sent to mock the living God.
Of a truth, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the nations and their lands,
and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone; therefore they were destroyed.
So now, O LORD our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the LORD.”
this is the word that the LORD has spoken concerning him:
‘Whom have you mocked and reviled?
By your servants you have mocked the Lord,
I dug wells
‘Have you not heard
while their inhabitants, shorn of strength,
‘I know your sitting down
Because you have raged against me
And the surviving remnant of the house of Judah shall again take root downward, and bear fruit upward;
for out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and out of Mount Zion a band of survivors. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will accomplish this.
By the way that he came, by the same he shall return, and he shall not come into this city, says the LORD.
For I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David.”
Then Sennach'erib king of Assyria departed, and went home and dwelt at Nin'eveh.

And as he was worshiping in the house of Nis'roch his god, Adram'melech and Share'zer, his sons, slew him with the sword, and escaped into the land of Ar'arat. And E'sar-had'don his son reigned in his stead.

In those days Hezeki'ah became sick and was at the point of death. And Isai'ah the prophet the son of A'moz came to him, and said to him, “Thus says the LORD: Set your house in order; for you shall die, you shall not recover.”
Then Hezeki'ah turned his face to the wall, and prayed to the LORD,
and said, “Remember now, O LORD, I beseech you, how I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in your sight.” And Hezeki'ah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the LORD came to Isai'ah:
“Go and say to Hezeki'ah, Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.
I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and defend this city.
Behold, I will make the shadow cast by the declining sun on the dial of A'haz turn back ten steps.” So the sun turned back on the dial the ten steps by which it had declined.
I said, In the noontide of my days
I said, I shall not see the LORD
My dwelling is plucked up and removed from me
I cry for help until morning;
Like a swallow or a crane I clamor,
But what can I say? For he has spoken to me,
O Lord, by these things men live,
Behold, it was for my welfare
For Sheol cannot thank you,
The living, the living, he thanks you,
The LORD will save me,
Now Isai'ah had said, “Let them take a cake of figs, and apply it to the boil, that he may recover.”
Hezeki'ah also had said, “What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the LORD?”
At that time Mer'odach-bal'adan the son of Bal'adan, king of Babylon, sent envoys with letters and a present to Hezeki'ah, for he heard that he had been sick and had recovered.

And Hezeki'ah welcomed them; and he showed them his treasure house, the silver, the gold, the spices, the precious oil, his whole armory, all that was found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his house or in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.

Then Isai'ah the prophet came to King Hezeki'ah, and said to him, “What did these men say? And from where did they come to you?” Hezeki'ah said, “They have come to me from a far country, from Babylon.”
He said, “What have they seen in your house?” Hezeki'ah answered, “They have seen all that is in my house; there is nothing in my storehouses that I did not show them.”
Behold, the days are coming, when all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have stored up till this day, shall be carried to Babylon; nothing shall be left, says the LORD.
And some of your own sons, who are born to you, shall be taken away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
Then said Hezeki'ah to Isai'ah, “The word of the LORD which you have spoken is good.” For he thought, “There will be peace and security in my days.”
Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
Speak tenderly to Jerusalem,
A voice cries:
Every valley shall be lifted up,
And the glory of the LORD shall be revealed,
A voice says, “Cry!”
The grass withers, the flower fades,
The grass withers, the flower fades;
Get you up to a high mountain,
Behold, the Lord GOD comes with might,
He will feed his flock like a shepherd,
Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand
Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD,
Whom did he consult for his enlightenment,
Behold, the nations are like a drop from a bucket,
Lebanon would not suffice for fuel,
All the nations are as nothing before him,
To whom then will you liken God,
The idol! a workman casts it,
He who is impoverished chooses for an offering
Have you not known? Have you not heard?
It is he who sits above the circle of the earth,
who brings princes to nought,
Scarcely are they planted, scarcely sown,
To whom then will you compare me,
Lift up your eyes on high and see:
Why do you say, O Jacob,
Have you not known? Have you not heard?
He gives power to the faint,
Even youths shall faint and be weary,
but they who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength,
Listen to me in silence, O islands;
Who stirred up one from the east
He pursues them and passes on safely,
Who has performed and done this,
The islands have seen and are afraid,
Every one helps his neighbor,
The craftsman encourages the goldsmith,
But you, Israel, my servant,
you whom I took from the ends of the earth,
fear not, for I am with you,
Behold, all who are incensed against you
You shall seek those who contend with you,
For I, the LORD your God,
Fear not, you worm Jacob,
Behold, I will make of you a threshing sledge,
you shall winnow them and the wind shall carry them away,
When the poor and needy seek water,
I will open rivers on the bare heights,
I will put in the wilderness the cedar,
that men may see and know,
Set forth your case, says the LORD;
Let them bring them, and tell us
Tell us what is to come hereafter,
Behold, you are nothing,
I stirred up one from the north, and he has come,
Who declared it from the beginning, that we might know,
I first have declared it to Zion,
But when I look there is no one;
Behold, they are all a delusion;
Behold my servant, whom I uphold,
He will not cry or lift up his voice,
a bruised reed he will not break,
He will not fail or be discouraged
Thus says God, the LORD,
“I am the LORD, I have called you in righteousness,
to open the eyes that are blind,
I am the LORD, that is my name;
Behold, the former things have come to pass,
Sing to the LORD a new song,
Let the desert and its cities lift up their voice,
Let them give glory to the LORD,
The LORD goes forth like a mighty man,
For a long time I have held my peace,
I will lay waste mountains and hills,
And I will lead the blind
They shall be turned back and utterly put to shame,
Hear, you deaf;
Who is blind but my servant,
He sees many things, but does not observe them;
The LORD was pleased, for his righteousness’ sake,
But this is a people robbed and plundered,
Who among you will give ear to this,
Who gave up Jacob to the spoiler,
So he poured upon him the heat of his anger
But now thus says the LORD, he who created you, O Jacob,
When you pass through the waters I will be with you;
For I am the LORD your God,
Because you are precious in my eyes,
Fear not, for I am with you;
I will say to the north, Give up,
every one who is called by my name,
Bring forth the people who are blind, yet have eyes,
Let all the nations gather together,
“You are my witnesses,” says the LORD,
I, I am the LORD,
I declared and saved and proclaimed,
“I am God, and also henceforth I am He;
Thus says the LORD,
I am the LORD, your Holy One,
Thus says the LORD,
who brings forth chariot and horse,
“Remember not the former things,
Behold, I am doing a new thing;
The wild beasts will honor me,
the people whom I formed for myself
“Yet you did not call upon me, O Jacob;
You have not brought me your sheep for burnt offerings,
You have not bought me sweet cane with money,
“I, I am He
Put me in remembrance, let us argue together;
Your first father sinned,
Therefore I profaned the princes of the sanctuary,
“But now hear, O Jacob my servant,
Thus says the LORD who made you,
For I will pour water on the thirsty land,
They shall spring up like grass amid waters,
This one will say, ‘I am the LORD’s,’
Thus says the LORD, the King of Israel
Who is like me? Let him proclaim it,
Fear not, nor be afraid;
Who fashions a god or casts an image, that is profitable for nothing?
Behold, all his fellows shall be put to shame, and the craftsmen are but men; let them all assemble, let them stand forth, they shall be terrified, they shall be put to shame together.

The carpenter stretches a line, he marks it out with a pencil; he fashions it with planes, and marks it with a compass; he shapes it into the figure of a man, with the beauty of a man, to dwell in a house.
He cuts down cedars; or he chooses a holm tree or an oak and lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest; he plants a cedar and the rain nourishes it.
Then it becomes fuel for a man; he takes a part of it and warms himself, he kindles a fire and bakes bread; also he makes a god and worships it, he makes it a graven image and falls down before it.
Half of it he burns in the fire; over the half he eats flesh, he roasts meat and is satisfied; also he warms himself and says, “Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire!”
And the rest of it he makes into a god, his idol; and falls down to it and worships it; he prays to it and says, “Deliver me, for you are my god!”

No one considers, nor is there knowledge or discernment to say, “Half of it I burned in the fire, I also baked bread on its coals, I roasted flesh and have eaten; and shall I make the residue of it an abomination? Shall I fall down before a block of wood?”
He feeds on ashes; a deluded mind has led him astray, and he cannot deliver himself or say, “Is there not a lie in my right hand?”
Remember these things, O Jacob,
I have swept away your transgressions like a cloud,
Sing, O heavens, for the LORD has done it;
Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer,
who frustrates the omens of liars,
who confirms the word of his servant,
who says to the deep, ‘Be dry,
who says of Cyrus, ‘He is my shepherd,
Thus says the LORD to his anointed, to Cyrus,
“I will go before you
I will give you the treasures of darkness
For the sake of my servant Jacob,
I am the LORD, and there is no other,
that men may know, from the rising of the sun
I form light and create darkness,
“Shower, O heavens, from above,
“Woe to him who strives with his Maker,
Woe to him who says to a father, ‘What are you begetting?’
Thus says the LORD,
I made the earth,
I have aroused him in righteousness,
Thus says the LORD:
Truly, you are a God who hide yourself,
All of them are put to shame and confounded,
But Israel is saved by the LORD
For thus says the LORD,
I did not speak in secret,
“Assemble yourselves and come,
Declare and present your case;
“Turn to me and be saved,
By myself I have sworn,
“Only in the LORD, it shall be said of me,
In the LORD all the offspring of Israel
Bel bows down, Nebo stoops,
They stoop, they bow down together,
“Listen to me, O house of Jacob,
even to your old age I am He,
“To whom will you liken me and make me equal,
Those who lavish gold from the purse,
They lift it upon their shoulders, they carry it,
“Remember this and consider,
remember the former things of old;
declaring the end from the beginning
calling a bird of prey from the east,
“Listen to me, you stubborn of heart,
I bring near my deliverance, it is not far off,
Come down and sit in the dust,
Take the millstones and grind meal,
Your nakedness shall be uncovered,
Our Redeemer—the LORD of hosts is his name—
Sit in silence, and go into darkness,
I was angry with my people,
You said, “I shall be mistress for ever,”
Now therefore hear this, you lover of pleasures,
These two things shall come to you
You felt secure in your wickedness,
But evil shall come upon you,
Stand fast in your enchantments
You are wearied with your many counsels;
Behold, they are like stubble,
Such to you are those with whom you have labored,
Hear this, O house of Jacob,
For they call themselves after the holy city,
“The former things I declared of old,
Because I know that you are obstinate,
I declared them to you from of old,
“You have heard; now see all this;
They are created now, not long ago;
You have never heard, you have never known,
“For my name’s sake I defer my anger,
Behold, I have refined you, but not like silver;
For my own sake, for my own sake, I do it,
“Listen to me, O Jacob,
My hand laid the foundation of the earth,
“Assemble, all of you, and hear!
I, even I, have spoken and called him,
Draw near to me, hear this:
Thus says the LORD,
O that you had listened to my commandments!
your offspring would have been like the sand,
Go forth from Babylon, flee from Chalde'a,
They thirsted not when he led them through the deserts;
“There is no peace,” says the LORD, “for the wicked.”
Listen to me, O islands,
He made my mouth like a sharp sword,
And he said to me, “You are my servant,
But I said, “I have labored in vain,
And now the LORD says,
he says:
Thus says the LORD,
Thus says the LORD:
saying to the prisoners, ‘Come forth,’
they shall not hunger or thirst,
And I will make all my mountains a way,
Behold, these shall come from afar,
Sing for joy, O heavens, and exult, O earth;
But Zion said, “The LORD has forsaken me,
“Can a woman forget her sucking child,
Behold, I have graven you on the palms of my hands;
Your builders outstrip your destroyers,
Lift up your eyes round about and see;
“Surely your waste and your desolate places
The children born in the time of your bereavement
Then you will say in your heart:
Thus says the Lord GOD:
Kings shall be your foster fathers,
Can the prey be taken from the mighty,
Surely, thus says the LORD:
I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh,
Thus says the LORD:
Why, when I came, was there no man?
I clothe the heavens with blackness,
The Lord GOD has given me
The Lord GOD has opened my ear,
I gave my back to those who struck me,
For the Lord GOD helps me;
he who vindicates me is near.
Behold, the Lord GOD helps me;
Who among you fears the LORD
Behold, all you who kindle a fire,
“Listen to me, you who pursue deliverance,
Look to Abraham your father
For the LORD will comfort Zion:
“Listen to me, my people,
My deliverance draws near speedily,
Lift up your eyes to the heavens,
“Listen to me, you who know righteousness,
For the moth will eat them up like a garment,
Awake, awake, put on strength,
Was it not you who dried up the sea,
And the ransomed of the LORD shall return,
“I, I am he who comforts you;
and have forgotten the LORD, your Maker,

For I am the LORD your God,
And I have put my words in your mouth,
Rouse yourself, rouse yourself,
There is none to guide her
These two things have befallen you—
Your sons have fainted,
Therefore hear this, you who are afflicted,
Thus says your Lord, the LORD,
and I will put it into the hand of your tormentors,
Awake, awake,
Shake yourself from the dust, arise,
For thus says the Lord GOD: My people went down at the first into Egypt to sojourn there, and the Assyrian oppressed them for nothing.
Now therefore what have I here, says the LORD, seeing that my people are taken away for nothing? Their rulers wail, says the LORD, and continually all the day my name is despised.
Therefore my people shall know my name; therefore in that day they shall know that it is I who speak; here am I.”
How beautiful upon the mountains
Listen, your watchmen lift up their voice,
Break forth together into singing,
The LORD has bared his holy arm
Depart, depart, go out from there,
For you shall not go out in haste,
Behold, my servant shall prosper,
As many were astonished at him —
so shall he startle many nations;
Who has believed what we have heard?
For he grew up before him like a young plant,
He was despised and rejected by men;
Surely he has borne our griefs
But he was wounded for our transgressions,
All we like sheep have gone astray;
He was oppressed, and he was afflicted,
By oppression and judgment he was taken away;
And they made his grave with the wicked
Yet it was the will of the LORD to bruise him;
he shall see the fruit of the travail of his soul and be satisfied;
Therefore I will divide him a portion with the great,
“Sing, O barren one, who did not bear;
Enlarge the place of your tent,
For you will spread abroad to the right and to the left,
“Fear not, for you will not be ashamed;
For your Maker is your husband,
For the LORD has called you
For a brief moment I forsook you,
In overflowing wrath for a moment
“For this is like the days of Noah to me:
For the mountains may depart
“O afflicted one, storm-tossed, and not comforted,
I will make your pinnacles of agate,

If any one stirs up strife,
Behold, I have created the smith
no weapon that is fashioned against you shall prosper,
“Ho, every one who thirsts,
Why do you spend your money for that which is not bread,
Incline your ear, and come to me;
Behold, I made him a witness to the peoples,
Behold, you shall call nations that you know not,
“Seek the LORD while he may be found,
let the wicked forsake his way,
For my thoughts are not your thoughts,
For as the heavens are higher than the earth,
“For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven,
so shall my word be that goes forth from my mouth;
“For you shall go out in joy,
Instead of the thorn shall come up the cypress;
Thus says the LORD:
Blessed is the man who does this,
Let not the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say,
For thus says the LORD:
I will give in my house and within my walls
“And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD,
